title: Need help for a Dogville analysis

commenti.body: I’m always ready to discuss this film! I feel there’s a lot of deeper meanings to peel back here. Would love to work on your project with you. (Hope this meets the comment character requirement eneenejksodjenelwlssksnsejwkslsns)

Ask yourself why the scene is there. You say it's important - what makes it so? What new understanding does it give about the characters, plot or ideas of the film? How does it make us rethink what came before, or how does it foreshadow what is to come? What is focused on in this scene that is symbolically or thematically meaningful for understanding the text as a whole?

Hope that helps. :-)

I re-watched the scene, it's difficult indeed to take more from it that its own efficiency (the suspense of the count, the image association with the people suspected to vote for her). I wonder why they gave you this scene.

That said, the gravity given to the moment, and of the music chosen there + the "punishment" associated with it (exile, exclusion from the community, possible death in the mountains....) + the vote, transforms it into a kinda of a trial. A judgement. And I suppose it's this side, in relation to the rest of the movie, that could be a way to enter and read the scene. Who judges Dogville, when and in which situation, is there a parallel with the judgement scene at the end when she judges them and decides to punish them all, etc.

Maybe the Bible can also help here. *Dogville* is pretty transparent on that parallel ("Dogville" = "Godville", "Grace" as a Jesus visiting human with kindness and living a kind of passion, returning to her "father" at the end, a father which before her was mean and revengeful to humans... the only difference being that, contrary to Jesus, she doesn't forgives humans after all). 

So in which part of the Bible is there a judgement, a trial, or Bells, is there a part which could be coherent with what we see here? My knowledge of the Bible is week, the only trial I know is the Pilate one, and the only vote the one proposed to the crowd about who to save. But it doesn't seem to really fit what we see here.

Also, the places chosen (old mine, exile in mountains) maybe suggest something. Dogville is also about proverty in America, and the economic crisis (there is a radio, gangsters, all that is coherent with the early 30's). Does poverty in the mountains or mines (abandonned ones) ring a bell on that? With the hobo imagery maybe? Once again, I don't know US enough to be sure.

Sorry, nothing sure or certain, but that would be the tracks I would follow!
Thank you so much, it really helps ! I will do my research following those tracks they are just perfect 👍
It does help, thank you ! This will help me start something !

Well if you have anything to say about this movie I'll gladly listen ! I feel the same, this movie is deep, but I only understand the surface if you know what I mean. I would love to hear about your opinion or interpretation of Dogville, anything even if it's unrelated to the sequence I have to analyze. I'm just genuinely interested in this movie !
